answer: Each new key is first refracted through a prism of uncorrelated evidence: writing cadence, grading timestamps, and who paid whom. If those bands collapse into one tight spectrum, the keys are merged as a single actor. Influence then grows only along a willow of slashable sponsorship—an established agent may extend just a few branches, and a later collision cuts the limb and the root deposit together. Until a key leaves the holding lagoon with a distinctive spectrum and intact sponsors, it has zero vote and zero emission, so a farm of labels bleeds stake instead of buying power.
